title: Initial Power Invariant
statement: For any bit string $z$, let $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ be the projections decoded from the self-delimiting pair encoding, with either projection set to the empty word when decoding fails, and let $\langle w\rangle$ be the natural number represented by a bit string with its first bit least significant. The state $\langle B,\langle N,\langle \operatorname{bits}(A\bmod B),\operatorname{bits}(1\bmod B)\rangle\rangle\rangle$, where $A=\pi_1(z)$, $N=\pi_1(\pi_2(z))$, and $B=\pi_2(\pi_2(z))$, has the following property: it can be written as $\langle B,\langle E,\langle b,\mathrm{acc}\rangle\rangle\rangle$ with $|E|\leq |\pi_1(\pi_2(z))|$, $b$ and $\mathrm{acc}$ in canonical binary form, $|b|\leq |A|+|B|$, and $|\mathrm{acc}|\leq 1+|B|$. If $\langle B\rangle>0$, then $\langle b\rangle,\langle\mathrm{acc}\rangle<\langle B\rangle$ and $\langle\mathrm{acc}\rangle\langle b\rangle^{\langle E\rangle}\equiv \langle A\rangle^{\langle N\rangle}\pmod{\langle B\rangle}$.
hypotheses_covered: z is an arbitrary bit string
If the decoded modulus is positive, the two residues are less than it and satisfy the stated congruence
